events.text:
**Recommendation: go to St. Joseph.** Fish spoons, rotators and flies in about 120 ft of water. Grand Haven is my second choice.

**My expected ratings for this week (0–4)**

| Port | Rating | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| St. Joseph | 3 (good) | Rated good on 2023-07-26 |
| Grand Haven | 2–3 | Rated good on 2023-07-19; not rated on 2023-07-26 |
| South Haven | 2 (average) | Rated average on 2023-07-26 |
| Muskegon | 2 (average) | Rated average on 2023-07-26, but hit or miss the week before |

**What the reports say.** The newest reports are from 2023-07-26, which is 6 days old. They are a guide, not current conditions.

- **St. Joseph**
  - "Salmon anglers continued to have good success." The most consistent water was about 120 ft (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26).
  - Spoons caught most of the fish, and rotators and flies also caught fish. Some fish came from 30 and 50 ft (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26).
  - The week before it was rated average, with a few fish in 100 ft and the fishing "slowing down" (St. Joseph, 2023-07-19).
- **Grand Haven**
  - Anglers caught a mixed bag of salmon and trout in 80–140 ft of water. Salmon were 60–120 ft down on orange or green spoons, and yellow or green meat rigs worked well (Grand Haven, 2023-07-26). That report was not rated.
  - The week before, it was rated good: 65–120 ft down in 130–220 ft of water, on yellow and green meat rigs and green flies. Glow spoons caught Chinook in low light (Grand Haven, 2023-07-19).
- **South Haven**
  - "Decent fishing" in about 110 ft of water, rated average. Rotators, flies and meat rigs did best (South Haven, 2023-07-26).
  - Earlier weeks were weaker. On 2023-07-19 the catch was mostly lake trout with some coho and steelhead, rated below average. On 2023-07-05 it was rated below average.
- **Muskegon**
  - Fair, rated average. The best action was 60–100 ft down in 90–150 ft of water, on green or glow spoons and green meat rigs (Muskegon, 2023-07-26).
  - It was "hit or miss" the week before, rated below average (Muskegon, 2023-07-19).

**Water.** The tool returned only a buoy summary this week. It gave no modeled cold-layer depths and no wind forecast.
- Buoy surface water, average for the week before 2023-08-01: St. Joseph 75 °F, South Haven 74 °F, Grand Haven and Muskegon 72 °F (buoy 45161).
- Surface temperatures were steady or falling slightly, and none showed an upwelling drop.
- I can't judge wind or wave conditions for a small boat. Check the marine forecast before you go.

**History (earlier seasons, same time of year).**
- In early August 2022, St. Joseph was rated good in both weeks I checked (St. Joseph, 2022-08-03 and 2022-08-10).
- In the same weeks of 2022, South Haven was rated below average on 2022-08-03. Its 2022-08-10 report was not rated, and the piers were closed for several days by red flag conditions.
- In 2022, Muskegon was rated good both weeks. Chinook were 55–130 ft down in 120–250 ft of water, and the bite was best in low light (Muskegon, 2022-08-03 and 2022-08-10).
- Grand Haven in 2022 was rated average (2022-08-03) and good (2022-08-10).

**My read**
- I'd expect St. Joseph to stay the best choice. It has the best latest rating and was also good in early August 2022.
- Grand Haven could match St. Joseph. Its latest report wasn't rated, but the report before it was good.
- I'd expect Muskegon to be average, with a chance of improving. Last year it was good in early August, and fishing in low light, with glow spoons, may help. This year's reports are only fair to hit or miss.
- I'd expect South Haven to be the weakest, since two of its last three reports were below average and one was average.
- These ratings are my inference from the DNR reports. They are not forecasts from the reports themselves.

**Caveats**
- Many reports mix salmon with lake trout, and the ports don't always separate them.
- Some ratings are "not rated", which I treated as a weak positive.
